primary_diagnosis: Choledocholithiasis / Biliary Calculi with Intermittent Obstructive Jaundice
secondary_diagnoses: Dehydration-Induced Urine Concentration exacerbating visible chromaturia
clinical_reasoning: Documented 2-month history of gallbladder/biliary calculus with prior jaundice. Current presentation of episodic dark yellow urine following heavy physical exertion in heat is a combination of transient biliary ductal obstruction (migrating calculus) and heat-induced concentrated dehydration. Repeating hepatobiliary imaging and liver enzymes is critical to confirm stone clearance versus persistent choledocholithiasis.
recommended_tests: Liver Function Tests (Total & Direct Bilirubin, AST, ALT, Alkaline Phosphatase)
Urine Routine and Microscopy (Urobilinogen & Bile Salts)
MRCP (Magnetic Resonance Cholangiopancreatography) if ductal dilatation is observed
